tone_statements.citation: Moyse-Faurie, Claire. 2020 [HAL deposit 2023, 'à paraître']. Dictionnaire xârâgurè-français. Lacito-CNRS. 156 pp. (1. Présentation; 2. Conventions d'écriture et phonologie; 3. Esquisse grammaticale; lexique). hal-04299485.
tone_statements.quote: Sur le plan linguistique, le xârâgurè appartient aux langues kanak du groupe Sud, tout comme l'ajië, le tîrî, le haméa et le xârâcùù. Ces langues ne sont pas tonales, contrairement aux langues parlées plus au nord ou plus au sud. Elles comportent toutes un nombre important de phonèmes, et une structure syllabique caractérisée par l'absence de consonnes finales, sauf dans des emprunts récents.
tone_statements.translation: Linguistically, Xârâgurè belongs to the Kanak languages of the South group, just like Ajië, Tîrî, Haméa and Xârâcùù. These languages are not tonal, unlike the languages spoken further north or further south. They all have a large number of phonemes, and a syllable structure characterised by the absence of final consonants, except in recent loanwords.
tone_statements.locator: §1 'Présentation', p. 5, last paragraph before §2 'Conventions d'écriture et phonologie'

sources.note: Nothing on accent/stress placement. Phonology section (§2.1, pp.6-9) covers syllable structure (C)V(C)V, 27 consonants, 17 short + 17 long vowels, vowel assimilation. §1 Présentation (p.5) states the South-group languages incl. xârâgurè 'ne sont pas tonales'. The word 'accent' occurs only in the orthographic sense (diacritics, alphabetical order).

tone.translation: Linguistically, Xârâgurè belongs to the Kanak languages of the South group, just like Ajië, Tîrî, Haméa and Xârâcùù. These languages are not tonal, unlike the languages spoken further north or further south. They all have a large number of phonemes, and a syllable structure characterised by the absence of final consonants, except in recent loanwords.
tone.says: Explicit first-hand statement that xârâgurè, like the other South-group Kanak languages (ajië, tîrî, haméa, xârâcùù), is NOT a tone language, in contrast to the languages spoken further north and further south; the phonology section (§2.1) then gives only segmental inventory (27 consonants, 17 short + 17 long vowels), syllable structure (C)V(C)V and vowel assimilation, with no tone or accent marking in the orthography (diacritics mark vowel quality/nasality, not pitch).

sources.citation: Lynch, John (abstracter), 'Xârâcùù', in Lynch, Ross & Crowley 2002, The Oceanic Languages, Richmond: Curzon, pp.765-775 (based on Moyse-Faurie 1995).
sources.note: Sister language Xârâcùù (xara1244) §1.3: 'Primary stress occurs on the initial syllable of any word with one, two or three syllables; with words of more than three syllables, stress occurs on the first two syllables.' Xaragure only named as the southern neighbour; no Xârâgurè statement.
